title: The TUI attention badge counts only the DISPLAYED team's watchdog holds and clears a stale badge on the first observation after arming

commands.observed: Bundled 36 modules; index.js 0.43 MB; git diff 7 insertions, 3 deletions in dist

contractTests: a FOREIGN team's hold neither warns nor raises the count
only the DISPLAYED team's holds are counted
the FIRST observation after arming publishes badgePanel(id, null) exactly once
a second IDENTICAL pass publishes nothing
tests.pageSideNoBadge: kept and green: 'the page publishes NO badge itself — the apply-side attention surface owns it (G2)' passes in the package run

changes.attentionBadge: filters workflow.holds to entries equal to workflow.team?.id; no team id means no hold count, so a foreign hold cannot warn or inflate unread
changes.armPanelAttention: adds a `settled` first-publish sentinel: the first observation publishes once even when the badge is null; the sentinel settles only on an acceptance or an absent badge member, preserving the existing refusal-retry semantics
changes.tests: fixture helper gained an optional teamId; the old workspace-wide-hold test now supplies the displayed id; three new tests added (foreign hold, displayed-only counting, first null publish, second identical no-publish) covering the four contract behaviors

notRun: node scripts/verify-dist-fresh.ts - excluded by the task instruction (cross-package dist-fresh gate is the captain/verifier's)
residualRisks: Dist freshness is not proven by the excluded cross-package gate; the rebuild used the pinned .toolchain bun 1.4.0 from the repo root and the resulting diff was inspected to contain exactly the two F5 changes.
The whole-wave gates (repo-wide verify:comments, docs, rows, manifest, test:qa) were not run in this lane; per-file comment coverage and the root typecheck passed.
Other writers' in-flight changes are present in the working tree; the diff produced by this lane is limited to the three declared files (git status scoped to packages/mpd-tui-plugin).
A duplicate entry of the displayed team id in `holds` counts twice (the count is membership-counted by design); the watchdog's own ledger does not emit duplicates today.
